blocks.x: A working build of Applied AI & GenAI for Reinsurance & Commercial Lines: the operating context that shapes it, the services sequenced through the method, and the deltas we commit to.

Reinsurance and specialty commercial books trade in complexity: treaty structures, cat exposure, bordereaux reconciliation and capital optimization. The data flows between cedants, reinsurers and brokers are still largely spreadsheets — which is why settlement cycles and model confidence suffer.

items: Specialty risks priced on judgment with variable evidence; appetite drifts by desk.
Ceded premium/loss bordereaux arrive in formats and qualities; reconciliation consumes analysts and hides data quality issues.

blocks.x: The pattern composes RAG & Enterprise Knowledge Systems, Enterprise AI Strategy & Roadmapping, AI Proof-of-Concept & Value Validation from the Applied AI & Generative AI tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Bordereaux intake/reconciliation, Treaty settlement, Retro/capacity optimization) on Dataq Compass and Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — Solvency II / RBC among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Answers with citations, not vibes: permission-aware retrieval over your regulated document estate.
Models that read scans, scenes and schematics: multimodal intelligence wired into operations.
Voice and avatar interfaces that resolve, not deflect — with emotion-aware escalation and full auditability.
Broker submissions summarized with appetite matching (turnaround in hours)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Insurance & Risk level this capability reads as: submissions summarized with citations to loss runs, exposure data and appetite rules (quote turnaround down 50% for SME lines). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

The cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability, and it does not flex by account. Weeks 1–2 belong to measurement: the baseline metric is captured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 run a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — steered by a control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 convert the pilot into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, and close with a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses a gate is stopped or redirected on the record.
